tools.name: refund_ticket_and_revoke_agent_access
tools.description: Issues a refund through Stripe for the charge tied to a support ticket, then removes the handling agent's access to that ticket. Returns the refund details after looking up the ticket.

params.name: agent_id
params.description: ID of the agent whose ticket access is removed

tools.code:
import sqlite3

import stripe
from agents import function_tool

stripe.api_key = "sk_live_placeholder"
DB_PATH = "support.db"


@function_tool
def refund_ticket_and_revoke_agent_access(ticket_id: str, amount_cents: int, agent_id: str) -> dict:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT charge_id, customer_email, status FROM tickets WHERE id = ?",
        (ticket_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    charge_id, customer_email, status = row

    refund = stripe.Refund.create(
        charge=charge_id,
        amount=amount_cents,
        metadata={"ticket_id": ticket_id, "agent_id": agent_id},
    )

    conn.execute(
        "DELETE FROM ticket_access WHERE ticket_id = ? AND agent_id = ?",
        (ticket_id, agent_id),
    )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()

    return {
        "ticket_id": ticket_id,
        "customer_email": customer_email,
        "previous_status": status,
        "refund_id": refund.id,
        "refund_status": refund.status,
        "amount_cents": amount_cents,
        "access_removed_for": agent_id,
    }

tools.name: run_escalation_job_and_assign_owner
tools.description: Runs the escalation script for a ticket and then makes the given team lead the ticket's owner. Returns whether the script succeeded.

params.name: ticket_id
params.description: ID of the ticket to escalate

params.name: lead_id
params.description: ID of the team lead who becomes owner

tools.code:
import sqlite3
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class EscalationResult:
    ticket_id: str
    exit_code: int
    new_owner: str
    output: str


def run_escalation_job_and_assign_owner(ticket_id: str, lead_id: str) -> EscalationResult:
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["python", "scripts/escalate.py", "--ticket", ticket_id],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=120,
    )
    conn = sqlite3.connect("support.db")
    conn.execute(
        "UPDATE ticket_owners SET owner_id = ? WHERE ticket_id = ?",
        (lead_id, ticket_id),
    )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    return EscalationResult(ticket_id, proc.returncode, lead_id, proc.stdout[-500:])

tools.name: send_ticket_transcript_and_purge_attachments
tools.description: Reads a ticket's attachment records, emails the ticket transcript to the customer, and then permanently deletes the ticket's attachment files and records.

params.name: customer_email
params.description: Customer email address to send the transcript to

tools.code:
import os
import smtplib
import sqlite3
from email.message import EmailMessage

from agents import function_tool


@function_tool
def send_ticket_transcript_and_purge_attachments(ticket_id: str, customer_email: str) -> str:
    conn = sqlite3.connect("support.db")
    messages = conn.execute(
        "SELECT author, body FROM messages WHERE ticket_id = ? ORDER BY created_at",
        (ticket_id,),
    ).fetchall()
    files = conn.execute(
        "SELECT path FROM attachments WHERE ticket_id = ?", (ticket_id,)
    ).fetchall()

    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = "support@example.com"
    msg["To"] = customer_email
    msg["Subject"] = f"Transcript for ticket {ticket_id}"
    msg.set_content("\n\n".join(f"{a}: {b}" for a, b in messages))
    with smtplib.SMTP("smtp.example.com", 587) as smtp:
        smtp.starttls()
        smtp.send_message(msg)

    for (path,) in files:
        os.remove(path)
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM attachments WHERE ticket_id = ?", (ticket_id,))
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    return f"Sent transcript and deleted {len(files)} attachments for {ticket_id}"

tools.name: archive_stale_ticket_exports
tools.description: Finds exported ticket files older than the given number of days, moves them into the archive folder, and deletes any empty export files. Returns counts of archived and deleted files.
tools.code:
import shutil
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("ticket-exports")


@dataclass
class ArchiveResult:
    archived: int
    deleted_empty: int
    archive_dir: str


@mcp.tool()
def archive_stale_ticket_exports(older_than_days: int, export_dir: str) -> ArchiveResult:
    source = Path(export_dir)
    archive = source / "archive"
    archive.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    cutoff = time.time() - older_than_days * 86400

    archived = 0
    deleted = 0
    for path in source.glob("*.csv"):
        stat = path.stat()
        if stat.st_size == 0:
            path.unlink()
            deleted += 1
            continue
        if stat.st_mtime < cutoff:
            shutil.move(str(path), str(archive / path.name))
            archived += 1

    return ArchiveResult(archived, deleted, str(archive))
